description: Evaluation of skill-lint. Each line in fixtures/leaky-skill/ is a line grepped on 2026-10-09 from real skills and rule files, with only the people, organizations, repos, clients and hosts replaced by consistent pseudonyms (nothing invented). Only the line order and file separators (frontmatter ---, blank lines, and the frontmatter name line the repo check requires) were added. The fixture lines are Japanese on purpose: they are real-world Japanese input. P12's email address and P13's home absolute path would trip this repo's own leak check (check-repo.py), so only the matching parts are stored as the tokens {{AT}} and {{USERS_DIR}}; the runner expands them into a temporary directory before linting (verbatim after expansion). lint uses generic regular expressions only; proper nouns such as people, organizations, clients and private bots are judged by the reviewer (no denylist). Group A (scripts/run_evals.py) grades lint.py results by lint_expect ⊆ actual and lint_forbid ∩ actual = ∅. Group B (scripts/run_reviewer_eval.py) counts recall over reviewer_expect (one element = one expected finding; a hit if the quote contains any of its words) and counts findings on negative lines as false positives (for N7, only findings containing reviewer_forbid_quote). A line is located by file and anchor (a fragment unique within the line); the leaking strings themselves are not written in evals.json. lint_expect_match lists strings that must appear in the match of that line's finding (to confirm which rule caught it).
